selection_rule: Every statement by an in-scope officeholder quoted in a story published on Nov. 18 or 19, 2026 in the NPR Politics and PBS NewsHour Politics feeds, as read on Nov. 19 at about 7:57 ET, less the stories earlier pages already used. No transcript from the fixed transcript sources was dated in that window; transcripts from Nov. 12 to 17 were searched only to confirm quotes, and none matched. PBS NewsHour carries Associated Press reporting. Quotes under five words were left out, as were commentators' accounts of what an official said and statements by officials outside the offices in scope. Statements are worded as the outlet reported them; entries beginning "Reported as" are the reporter's wording.
lede: Wednesday's political news centered on three threads. House Democrats nominated Hakeem Jeffries for speaker. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin testified to a House committee about last week's string of technology outages and about his flight to a college football game the day after the Nov. 13 nationwide ground stop. President Trump traveled through Asia to a three-way meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen.

Senators also spoke on the final Senate count after the Alaska race was called, on Sen. Bernie Sanders's plan for Medicare for All, and on Sen. John Cornyn's decision to block a Justice Department official nominated to a federal court seat in Texas. Rep. Mike Lawler, who lost his re-election bid, talked about the coming funding deadline and about guardrails for artificial intelligence.

This page lists 78 statements by 17 officeholders. Thirty-four made a checkable factual claim, or rested a prediction on one, and every one of them was checked. Most of the checks turned on a single official document: the FAA's account of the ground stop, a GAO report on AI platforms, the CMS health spending figures, the Senate's cloture rule. The rest relied on news reports where no primary record was available, and each finding says which applies.

statements.speaker: Markwayne Mullin
statements.context: At a House Homeland Security hearing on Nov. 18, Mullin explained why he did not cancel his Saturday flight to the LSU-Texas game after the nationwide ground stop.
statements.quote: If we canceled something with the airspace completely open, it could bring confusion
statements.test: True if FAA records show the Nov. 13 nationwide ground stop had been lifted and the national airspace was open to normal traffic before Mullin's flight on Saturday, Nov. 14. False if FAA records show the ground stop or a nationwide traffic restriction still in effect when the flight departed. Cannot be determined if the flight time or the time the restrictions ended cannot be established from records.
statements.premise: The national airspace had fully reopened when Mullin's Saturday, Nov. 14 flight to the LSU-Texas game took place, after the Nov. 13 nationwide ground stop.
statements.finding: As reported by NPR and the AP citing the FAA, the Nov. 13 nationwide ground stop ended around 8:15 p.m. ET that Friday; CNN reports Mullin's Coast Guard jet landed in Baton Rouge on Saturday night, nearly a day later. The FAA's own records were not read directly.

evidence.label: NPR via WAMC, FAA lifts the nationwide ground stop
AP via HuffPost, Mullin defends using government plane
CNN, Mullin and the FAA ground stop
New York Post, Mullin defends flight

statements.speaker: Markwayne Mullin
statements.context: Mullin told a House hearing on Nov. 18 why he would have been at the LSU-Texas game in Louisiana, which he flew to after the nationwide ground stop.
statements.quote: I was meeting the governor there.
statements.test: True if a public record (the Louisiana governor's schedule or statement, or contemporaneous reporting of the event) shows Mullin met Louisiana's governor at or around the Nov. 14 LSU-Texas game. False if the governor's office or a record shows no meeting was planned or held. Cannot be determined if no record speaks to it.
statements.finding: No schedule or statement from Gov. Jeff Landry's office and no report of a meeting at the game was found; reports place Mullin in a private box with tickets obtained through Rep. Steve Scalise. The record neither shows a meeting nor shows that none was planned.

evidence.label: New York Daily News (AP), Mullin congressional hearing
New York Post, Mullin defends flight

statements.speaker: Markwayne Mullin
statements.context: Mullin described how flights already in the air were landed when the Nov. 13 nationwide FAA ground stop began, at a House Homeland Security hearing on Nov. 18.
statements.quote: We landed over 4,000 planes when the ground stoppage went out because of the communication and didn't have one single incident.
statements.test: True if FAA or other official figures show more than 4,000 airborne aircraft were landed after the Nov. 13 ground stop began, with no reported accident or incident. False if official figures show fewer than 4,000, or an accident or incident was reported during that period. Cannot be determined if no official count has been published.

also_said.quote: We landed over 4,000 planes when the ground stoppage went out because of the communication, and didn't have one single incident.

statements.finding: The FAA's Nov. 15 Q&A says "approximately 3,500 aircraft safely landed" when the ground stop was implemented, below the more than 4,000 stated, and that every passenger arrived safely. The FAA figure is approximate, and the FAA and L3Harris investigation into the root cause is still open.

evidence.label: FAA, Nationwide Ground Stop Questions and Answers

statements.speaker: Markwayne Mullin
statements.context: Mullin assessed the response to the nationwide FAA ground stop, saying planes were landed without incident, at a House Homeland Security hearing on Nov. 18.
statements.quote: That in itself is a great success

statements.speaker: Markwayne Mullin
statements.context: Questioned at a House hearing on Nov. 18 about his flight to the LSU game after the ground stop, Mullin said when the trip had been scheduled.
statements.quote: I took my family and my great-nieces to an LSU game that was scheduled for weeks prior to that
statements.test: True if the LSU-Texas game date, or Mullin's planned attendance, was on record at least two weeks before Nov. 14. False if both the game date and the trip were set only in the days before. Cannot be determined if neither can be dated from a record.
statements.finding: LSU's schedule release of Dec. 11, 2025 listed Texas at Tiger Stadium on Nov. 14, 2026, about 11 months before the game. When Mullin's own trip was planned is not on any independent record.

evidence.label: LSU Sports, 2026 home schedule release

statements.speaker: Markwayne Mullin
statements.context: AP reported what Mullin said on Nov. 17 and 18 about the government plane and the cost of his flight to the LSU-Texas game.
statements.quote: Reported as: Mullin had said Tuesday and reiterated Wednesday that he is required to fly on government planes and that he personally paid for the trip.
statements.test: True if DHS or federal travel rules require the Secretary of Homeland Security to fly on government aircraft and a record shows Mullin paid for the trip's personal portion. False if the rules let the secretary fly commercially for personal travel, or a record shows he did not pay. Cannot be determined if the rule or the payment record is not public.
statements.finding: DHS told CNN that Mullin was "required by law" to use a government plane and pays personally for non-official flights, but no statute or DHS policy text and no payment or reimbursement record was found. The claim rests only on Mullin's and DHS's own statements.

evidence.label: CNN, DHS statement on Mullin's flight
AP via HuffPost, Mullin defends using government plane

statements.speaker: Markwayne Mullin
statements.context: At a House Homeland Security hearing on Nov. 18, Mullin gave his level of confidence about the cause of the week's technology outages and nationwide ground stop.
statements.quote: I'm 98 percent confident that this has nothing to do with our adversaries hacking or going after our systems.

statements.speaker: Markwayne Mullin
statements.context: AP reported what Mullin told the public at a White House news conference with Transportation Secretary Duffy on Nov. 13, the day of the nationwide ground stop.
statements.quote: Reported as: During a news conference Friday with Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy at the White House, he pushed for more funding for the aging air traffic control system while also assuring the public that the government was not seeing any signs of a deliberate cyberattack.
statements.test: True if official accounts (FAA, DHS, CISA) to date report no evidence of a deliberate cyberattack behind the Nov. 13 ground stop. False if an official account reports evidence of a deliberate cyberattack. Cannot be determined if no official account addresses the cause.
statements.finding: The FAA's Nov. 15 Q&A says "we have no indication that this was a cyberattack or an outside nefarious actor" and traces the stop to data flooding its telecommunications network from sites in Amarillo, Texas, and El Dorado, Arkansas. The root-cause investigation is still open.

evidence.label: FAA, Nationwide Ground Stop Questions and Answers

statements.speaker: Markwayne Mullin
statements.context: Questioned on Nov. 18 about immigration enforcement and ICE, Mullin described the Department of Homeland Security's current enforcement policy.
statements.quote: Our policy right now is to go after the worst of the worst.
statements.test: True if DHS or ICE published policy or ICE's own arrest and detention data show enforcement concentrated on people with serious criminal convictions or charges. False if ICE's own data show most people arrested or detained have no criminal conviction or pending charge. Cannot be determined if no official policy or data from the current period speak to it.
statements.finding: AskAmerica's ICE detention data (TRAC compilation of ICE figures, snapshot of July 11, 2026) show 19,329 of 65,765 detainees convicted and 20,247 with pending charges, about 60% combined; an American Immigration Council analysis of ICE arrest data found most at-large arrests in December 2025 and January 2026 involved people with no criminal record. "Worst of the worst" has no defined threshold, so the evidence does not decide the claim.

evidence.label: crime.ice_detention_population_by_criminality (July 11, 2026 snapshot)
evidence.sql: SELECT snapshot_date, criminality, detained_population FROM crime.ice_detention_population_by_criminality WHERE arresting_agency='Total' ORDER BY snapshot_date DESC, criminality FETCH FIRST 12 ROWS ONLY

evidence.label: American Immigration Council, analysis of ICE arrest data

statements.speaker: Markwayne Mullin
statements.context: Mullin explained to a House committee on Nov. 18 why immigration enforcement arrests include people beyond the targeted individual.
statements.quote: So, when we arrest someone that's on a warrant, most of the time, they're not by themselves.
statements.test: True if an official source (ICE data, DHS or inspector general report) shows that most warrant-based arrests encounter other people with the target. False if official data show most such arrests find the target alone. Cannot be determined if no official data describe who is present at arrests.
statements.finding: No official ICE, DHS or inspector general source found describes who is present at warrant-based arrests. Secondary analyses of ICE data put "collateral" arrests at about a quarter of ICE arrests, which is a different measure from the one the statement makes.

evidence.label: American Immigration Council, analysis of ICE arrest data

statements.speaker: Sean Duffy
statements.context: AP reported what Duffy said on Nov. 18 about who was responsible for the router problem behind the Nov. 13 nationwide FAA ground stop.
statements.quote: Reported as: Duffy said on "The Morning Meeting" show Wednesday that a contractor failed to identify and isolate the router issue that caused the weekend ground stop quickly enough.
statements.test: True if the FAA or another official investigative account finds the contractor (L3Harris) failed to identify and isolate the router problem quickly enough. False if an official account places the delay or responsibility elsewhere. Cannot be determined if the official investigation has not yet assigned responsibility.
statements.finding: No FAA or other official investigative account has assigned responsibility for the router problem; the AP reports investigators are still weighing installer misconfiguration against faulty equipment, and the router maker's owner says the device worked as configured. AskAmerica's FAA advisory data show the national ground stop issued and cancelled on Nov. 13, with no cause recorded.

evidence.label: transport.faa_atcscc_advisories (Nov. 13-14, 2026 ground stop advisories)
evidence.sql: SELECT advisory_date, advisory_number, facility, subject, sent_time_utc FROM transport.faa_atcscc_advisories WHERE advisory_date BETWEEN '2026-11-13' AND '2026-11-14' AND (advisory_type='GROUND_STOP' OR subject LIKE '%NATIONWIDE%' OR subject LIKE '%ALL%') ORDER BY sent_time_utc FETCH FIRST 30 ROWS ONLY

evidence.label: AP via Chicago Tribune, Duffy blames L3Harris

statements.speaker: Sean Duffy

statements.speaker: Marco Rubio
statements.context: AP reported Rubio's statement to reporters during President Trump's Asia trip on Nov. 18 about whether the week's technology outages were connected or caused by outside actors.
statements.quote: Reported as: Rubio told reporters there was "zero" evidence that the outages were connected or were tied to rival nations, cyber hackers or criminals.
statements.test: True if official accounts of each of the week's outages (the FAA ground stop, Microsoft, the banks, the NSA) report non-malicious causes and no link among them. False if an official account reports a link among the outages or a hostile nation, hacker or criminal behind one. Cannot be determined if the causes have not been officially published.
statements.finding: The accounts found for each outage are non-malicious and none links them: Microsoft cites a latent software defect, JPMorgan Chase "a software bug" that "is not cyber-related," the NSA "temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance," and the FAA network data flooding. The NSA gave no further cause, the FAA account was not read from its primary document in this check, and Microsoft's final report was still pending, so the evidence does not fully decide the claim.

evidence.label: AP via FOX19, NSA communications network outage
Al Jazeera, what caused the Chase outage
ITPro, Microsoft 365 outage root cause
WEAR-TV, nationwide disruptions

statements.speaker: Marco Rubio
statements.context: Rubio, speaking on Nov. 18, explained how fixing a software vulnerability can itself cause the kind of technology outages seen that week.
statements.quote: Sometimes when you are going in to fix your system because you've identified a vulnerability, it creates a short-term disruption
statements.test: True if an official or vendor incident report documents a fix for an identified vulnerability, or the remediation work itself, causing a short-term outage (in general, or in one of the week's outages). False if no such case is on record. Cannot be determined if records describe outages during maintenance without saying whether the work addressed a vulnerability.
statements.finding: Microsoft's support article KB5025885 says its fix for the Secure Boot vulnerability CVE-2023-24932 "could cause issues for some device boot configurations" and lists known issues from applying it, including devices that fail to boot and BitLocker recovery prompts, with recovery steps. No outage from the week of Nov. 12-18 is documented as caused by a vulnerability fix.

evidence.label: Microsoft, KB5025885 Windows Boot Manager revocations for CVE-2023-24932
AP via FOX19, NSA communications network outage

statements.speaker: Donald Trump
statements.context: Trump spoke on Nov. 17 about the prospects for ending Russia's war in Ukraine, ahead of his planned meetings with Putin and Xi.
statements.quote: I think it's very close to getting it done

statements.speaker: Donald Trump
statements.context: AP reported Trump's Nov. 17 explanation of why Russia's war in Ukraine might now be resolved.
statements.quote: Reported as: But Trump said on Tuesday that the deaths of tens of thousands of Russian troops every month had created an opening to resolve the conflict.
statements.test: True if official or independent estimates (U.S., U.K. Ministry of Defence, Ukrainian General Staff, or published studies) put Russian troops killed at tens of thousands per month in recent months. False if those estimates put deaths well below 20,000 a month. Cannot be determined if the estimates give only total casualties (killed and wounded) and cannot separate deaths.
statements.finding: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said in January 2026 that 20,000 to 25,000 Russian soldiers are killed each month, excluding the seriously wounded, while U.K. Ministry of Defence figures combine killed and wounded and other estimates found in search put deaths near 9,000 a month. The estimates straddle the line the test draws, so they do not decide it.

evidence.label: UNITED24 Media, NATO says Russia loses up to 25,000 soldiers killed per month

statements.speaker: Donald Trump
statements.context: AP reported what Trump said after his Nov. 18 lunch meeting with Philippine President Marcos in Manila about a U.S.-Philippines trade agreement.
statements.quote: Reported as: He said after their meeting that the two nations had reached a trade deal on Wednesday, though he had also said last year that an agreement had been reached.

False if either government states no agreement was reached that day. Cannot be determined if only verbal claims exist and no document has been released.
statements.finding: Neither the White House statements page (current through Nov. 17) nor USTR's press releases (current through Nov. 18) carried a U.S.-Philippines trade document, and neither government has said no deal was reached; an AP report dates a signing to Tuesday, Nov. 17. Only verbal accounts of the agreement were found.

USTR press releases

statements.speaker: Donald Trump
statements.context: In a September remarks played by NPR, Trump described the position of the United States relative to China in artificial intelligence.
statements.topic: AI and chip exports to China
statements.quote: We're leading China in AI. We're the most sophisticated country in the world.
statements.test: True if standard published measures (for example the Stanford AI Index on notable models, private investment and compute) show the United States ahead of China in AI. False if they show China ahead on most of them. Cannot be determined if the measures split. 'Most sophisticated country in the world' is an opinion and is not assessed.
statements.finding: Stanford's 2026 AI Index shows the U.S. ahead on top-tier models and on private AI investment ($285.9 billion in 2025 against China's $12.4 billion), though it says the model performance gap "has effectively closed," with a 2.7% U.S. lead in March 2026; China leads on publications, citations and patents. "Most sophisticated country in the world" is an opinion and was not assessed.

evidence.label: Stanford HAI, 2026 AI Index Report

statements.speaker: Donald Trump
statements.context: AP reported Trump's statement about the Justice Department lawsuit seeking to block certification of the Alaska Senate race if the incumbent lost.
statements.quote: Reported as: The Department of Justice filed a lawsuit that Trump said he ordered.
statements.test: True if court records show the Justice Department filed a suit concerning certification of the Alaska Senate race and a statement by Trump himself (post or remarks) says he directed it. False if no such suit was filed or Trump's own statement says otherwise. Cannot be determined if whether he ordered it rests only on secondhand accounts.
statements.finding: The Justice Department filed United States v. State of Alaska (D. Alaska, 3:26-cv-00376) on Oct. 22, 2026, seeking to block certification of Senate results it said were tainted by a second Dan Sullivan on the ballot; the court dismissed it Nov. 1 and the department appealed. The AP reports Trump told reporters on Oct. 23, "I'm the one that said do it"; no video or transcript of the remarks was read.

evidence.label: Justice Department complaint, U.S. v. State of Alaska
Democracy Docket, case page and docket history
AP via WDBJ7, Trump administration files lawsuit

statements.speaker: Chuck Schumer
statements.context: Schumer, the Senate Democratic leader, commented in a social media statement on Democrats' final seat count after the Alaska Senate race was called.
